reasons: The maximal quotient is decided through exact comparisons for every unordered graph pair.
Full quotienting requires graph-pair signatures rather than signatures relative only to one reference graph.
The accepted domain now contains every finite syntactically valid oracle problem, including unrealizable or graph-infeasible inputs that receive rejection certificates.

correct: Realizability and existence of an admissible DAG are now decided by the algorithm. A rational table and compressed graph family can be optional checked accelerators but cannot remain mathematical acceptance assumptions.
The algorithm is corrected atomically to decide realizability, build all tied DAGs, and return the maximal quotient with pairwise certificates.

correct: The corrected procedure must decide model nonemptiness, enumerate all admissible minimum-edge ties by default, and compute the full pairwise effect quotient with equality and positive-separator certificates.
The complete family must be computable without a supplied compressed representation.

correct: The tied minimum-edge family must be constructed completely from the finite vertex set, background orientations, and exact CI oracle; a supplied SA-MPDAG or CPDAG representation is only an optional validated compression.
target-estimand-replace: The strengthened output retains the graph-indexed causal query and reports its maximal equality quotient rather than presupposing a single common value.
estimand-functional-replace: The functional line must distinguish classwise identification from the one-class common-effect special case.
comparator-promise-table-replace: The comparator table now records the maximal quotient result and removes the unsupported extensional-equivalence promise with single-MPDAG theory.
The DAG family is now defined by exhaustive finite enumeration, independently of whether a compressed graph family is supplied.
The reference graph exists only after the exhaustive graph stage has produced a nonempty tied family.
The graph family is an optional compressed enumeration certificate rather than a required input.
The procedure now returns preliminary rejection certificates or the maximal effect quotient, not merely a reference common-effect-or-separator decision.
The rational table is retained only as an optional fast-path certificate and is no longer required for oracle realizability.
The input is syntactically certified without assuming real or rational oracle realizability and without requiring a supplied graph family.
The theorem's claim and proof basis are retargeted to the realizability-first, exhaustive-enumeration, maximal-quotient procedure and its reduced comparison count.

narrow: After removal of the supplied rational realization and supplied graph family as domain assumptions, the old universal two-output claim is too strong because it presupposes a nonempty oracle model and a nonempty graph family. The replacement narrows causal-output guarantees to the explicitly nonempty case, adds exact rejection certificates otherwise, drops all complexity and height promises, and within the valid case reports the directive's maximal effect quotient.

verdict.note: Accepted all 13 items after high math review: finite syntax-only domain, exact rejection certificates, exhaustive tied-DAG construction, maximal quotient, correct normalized-coordinate bounds, and honest metadata.
